account: In replies under the Right to Information Act dated 25 July 2022, Delhi Police said that it treats face matches below 80 percent similarity as false positives that need corroborative evidence. Those replies do not name the software. On the evening of 17 March 2025, cash courier Ajmal Bhai Ganesh, 49, of R K Enterprises was robbed at gunpoint of Rs 80 lakh near his home in Fatehpuri, Chandni Chowk, Delhi. Delhi Police's North district analyzed footage from some 500 closed-circuit television cameras. Israeli facial recognition software matched a frame of a man who had followed the victim to a record at Kotwali police station, with a similarity of 32.09 percent. The match gave police the name of Mohammad Ali, 21, of Daryaganj. No source says whether the 80 percent rule applies to the Israeli system, and this match falls below that line. Police confirmed Ali's role by arresting and questioning him. He was arrested early on 19 March (the Times of India says Tuesday) and named Samir, 19, who was arrested in Daryaganj. A raid on Samir's home found Rs 79.5 lakh and a semi-automatic pistol, and police called the cash the entire amount.

ai_role.statement: By DCP (North) Raja Banthia's account, teams took a screengrab of a man seen following the victim. The Israeli software matched it to a prior record from Kotwali police station with a similarity score of 32.09 percent. That gave them Ali's name and his Daryaganj address. A score that low is a lead, not an identification. Police confirmed it by laying a trap and interrogating Ali. The auto-rickshaw trace, the reconnaissance evidence and Samir's arrest came from conventional work. The reports name neither the software nor its vendor.

fields.account: In replies under the Right to Information Act dated 25 July 2022, Delhi Police said that it treats face matches below 80 percent similarity as false positives that need corroborative evidence. Those replies do not name the software. On the evening of 17 March 2025, cash courier Ajmal Bhai Ganesh, 49, of R K Enterprises was robbed at gunpoint of Rs 80 lakh near his home in Fatehpuri, Chandni Chowk, Delhi. Delhi Police's North district analyzed footage from some 500 closed-circuit television cameras. Israeli facial recognition software matched a frame of a man who had followed the victim to a record at Kotwali police station, with a similarity of 32.09 percent. The match gave police the name of Mohammad Ali, 21, of Daryaganj. No source says whether the 80 percent rule applies to the Israeli system, and this match falls below that line. Police confirmed Ali's role by arresting and questioning him. He was arrested early on 19 March (the Times of India says Tuesday) and named Samir, 19, who was arrested in Daryaganj. A raid on Samir's home found Rs 79.5 lakh and a semi-automatic pistol, and police called the cash the entire amount.
fields.summary: Israeli facial recognition software, unnamed in the reports, matched a robbery suspect's camera image to a police record; two arrested within about a day and Rs 79.5 lakh of the Rs 80 lakh recovered.

must_hold: A low-similarity match (32.09 percent) is only a lead and must be confirmed by conventional investigation before arrest
The suspect must already be in the database; a first-time offender would not have been matched
produced_by: Dense CCTV coverage (about 500 cameras across five areas) from which a usable frame of the suspect's face could be taken
A police facial recognition database that already held the suspect's photograph from a prior arrest at Kotwali police station

purpose: The software was deployed to identify people in CCTV footage by matching faces against police databases. Naming a robbery suspect from a frame is that function.

ratings.reason: The recovered Rs 79.5 lakh belonged to the courier's employer, R K Enterprises, and the reports describe no outcome for Ajmal Bhai Ganesh himself.

R K Enterprises got back Rs 79.5 lakh of the Rs 80 lakh taken at gunpoint, which police described as the entire amount. Delhi Police's North district cleared, within about 24 hours, an armed robbery whose video had gone viral. Both accused are in judicial custody under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Arms Act, and police recovered the pistol.
Two men who had watched cash couriers and used a firearm were arrested. The reports give no evidence that further robberies were prevented, so the extent of any public benefit cannot be established.
